newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says foreign media ownership seen high.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says foreign media ownership seen high.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard responded to a call for higher foreign ownership limits in media companies by saying there was already a strong view that current levels were quite high.
"I think there is a strong feeling that the level of foreign ownership in the Australian media is already quite high," Howard told Melbourne radio on Tuesday.
Earlier on Tuesday, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chief Allan Fels urged the government to review its laws limiting foreign ownership of the Australian media.
The government is reviewing media ownership laws, but has said its review does not cover foreign ownership.
Canadian media baron Conrad Black has said he would consider selling out of newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd if he cannot lift his present 25 percent stake to 50 percent.
Australia's media rules prevent foreigners from holding more than 25 percent of a newspaper group and more than 15 percent of a television company.
Communications Minister Richard Alston last week ruled out widening the government's media industry review to include foreign ownership.
Treasurer Peter Costello also said he saw no need to change foreign ownership limits.
